subproblem.title: Symmetry of the second derivative of a C² map (Schwarz)
subproblem.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ, every f : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ (ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) and every x ∈ ℝⁿ such that f is C² at x (ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x), the second derivative L := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x is symmetric: L a b = L b a for all a, b ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn N) (x : Rn n), ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x → ∀ a b : Rn n, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x a b = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x b a
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 ("ψ is C² on the open set V ∋ x, so ContDiffAt ℝ 2 ψ x and its second derivative at x is symmetric: S_x(a, b) = S_x(b, a) (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, with minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2)"). The cited Mathlib lemma lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric, which is not in the import closure of the frozen contract, and a leaf may not add imports; this child therefore supplies the classical proof of Schwarz's theorem from the mean value inequality and the chain rule, which are available.
Notation. Df(y) := fderiv ℝ f y ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) and L := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x ∈ L(ℝⁿ, L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ)); L is linear in each argument, so L(ta)(tb) = t² L a b. Norms of linear maps are operator norms.
1. (Regularity.) Since f is C² at x and 2 ≠ ∞, f is C² on a neighbourhood of x (ContDiffAt.eventually), in particular differentiable at every point of a neighbourhood of x. Moreover y ↦ Df(y) is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.fderiv_right with 1 + 1 ≤ 2), hence differentiable at x: Df has Fréchet derivative L at x.
2. (Uniform first-order expansion.) Let ε > 0. By step 1 there is δ > 0 such that for every h ∈ ℝⁿ with ‖h‖ < δ: f is differentiable at x + h, and ‖Df(x + h) − Df(x) − L h‖ ≤ ε‖h‖ (the little-o characterisation of the derivative L of Df at x, hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero and Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff, combined with the eventual differentiability via Metric.eventually_nhds_iff).
3. (An auxiliary curve.) Fix a, b ∈ ℝⁿ and t > 0 with t(‖a‖ + ‖b‖) < δ. For s ∈ [0, 1] put h₁(s) := ta + (st)b and h₂(s) := (st)b. Then ‖h₁(s)‖ ≤ t‖a‖ + st‖b‖ ≤ t(‖a‖ + ‖b‖) < δ and ‖h₂(s)‖ ≤ t‖b‖ ≤ t(‖a‖ + ‖b‖) < δ. Define g : ℝ → ℝᴺ by g(s) := f(x + h₁(s)) − f(x + h₂(s)) − s · L(ta)(tb). The curves s ↦ x + h_j(s) have velocity tb, and f is differentiable at x + h_j(s) by step 2, so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) g is differentiable at every s ∈ [0, 1] with g′(s) = Df(x + h₁(s))(tb) − Df(x + h₂(s))(tb) − L(ta)(tb).
4. (Derivative bound.) For s ∈ [0, 1] let R_j := Df(x + h_j(s)) − Df(x) − L h_j(s) (j = 1, 2). Since h₁(s) − h₂(s) = ta and L is linear, R₁(tb) − R₂(tb) = Df(x + h₁(s))(tb) − Df(x + h₂(s))(tb) − L(ta)(tb) = g′(s). By step 2, ‖R_j‖ ≤ ε‖h_j(s)‖ ≤ εt(‖a‖ + ‖b‖), and ‖tb‖ = t‖b‖, so ‖g′(s)‖ ≤ ‖R₁‖‖tb‖ + ‖R₂‖‖tb‖ ≤ 2εt²(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)‖b‖.
5. (Mean value inequality.) By the mean value inequality on [0, 1] (norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment_01'), ‖g(1) − g(0)‖ ≤ 2εt²(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)‖b‖. Now g(1) − g(0) = Δ − t² L a b, where Δ := f(x + (ta + tb)) − f(x + tb) − (f(x + ta) − f(x)). Hence ‖Δ − t² L a b‖ ≤ 2εt²(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)‖b‖.
6. (Symmetrisation.) Δ does not change when a and b are exchanged (ta + tb = tb + ta), and t(‖b‖ + ‖a‖) < δ, so step 5 applied to (b, a) gives ‖Δ − t² L b a‖ ≤ 2εt²(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)‖a‖. Since t²(L a b − L b a) = (Δ − t² L b a) − (Δ − t² L a b), the triangle inequality gives t²‖L a b − L b a‖ ≤ 2εt²(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)(‖a‖ + ‖b‖) ≤ 4εt²(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)². The choice t := δ/(2(‖a‖ + ‖b‖ + 1)) > 0 satisfies t(‖a‖ + ‖b‖) < δ; dividing by t² > 0 yields ‖L a b − L b a‖ ≤ 4ε(‖a‖ + ‖b‖)².
7. (Conclusion.) The bound of step 6 holds for every ε > 0 (δ depended on ε, the final bound does not), so ‖L a b − L b a‖ = 0 (le_of_forall_pos_le_add), i.e. fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x a b = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x b a. ∎
Formalization note. Only the frozen imports are needed: Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue is in the import closure of GMT.Ch02.Submission, Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric is not (do not cite IsSymmSndFDerivAt). Useful names: ContDiffAt.eventually, ContDiffAt.fderiv_right, hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero, Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff, Metric.eventually_nhds_iff, HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt, norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment_01', ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, sub_apply, add_apply, FunLike.coe_smul, le_of_forall_pos_le_add. A Lean proof following steps 1–7 (about 140 lines) compiled warning-free against the frozen contract with only `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` and axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: f is C² near x and Df has derivative L = D²f(x) at x, so ‖Df(x+h) − Df(x) − L h‖ ≤ ε‖h‖ for ‖h‖ < δ.
For g(s) = f(x+ta+stb) − f(x+stb) − s·L(ta)(tb), g′(s) = R₁(tb) − R₂(tb) with ‖R_j‖ ≤ εt(‖a‖+‖b‖).
Mean value inequality: ‖Δ − t²L a b‖ ≤ 2εt²(‖a‖+‖b‖)‖b‖ for the second difference Δ, which is symmetric in a, b.
Exchanging a and b and dividing by t² gives ‖L a b − L b a‖ ≤ 4ε(‖a‖+‖b‖)² for every ε > 0, so L a b = L b a.
